Forecast Discussion

High pressure building into the Northeast wedges down the east side of the Appalachians through the weekend. It’s a “dry wedge”: cool but not dramatically so, as dry weather holds.

The cool wedge erodes early Monday, allowing afternoon temperatures to rise Monday and Tuesday, but overnight temperatures remain chilly in the valleys for a few days.

Low pressure develops over the Bahamas as high pressure remains over the Appalachians. An easterly flow between the two adds some clouds Wednesday and Thursday, but nothing spoils an overall pleasant end to October. Maybe we get some light rain here early in the following week.
